provenance: Selected code inspections by Codex; technical notes, not independent human ballots or vulnerability ground truth.
selection: Purposive cases covering format-family-only matches and distinct Unknown failure mechanisms; no population error-rate inference.

cases.note: Query builds a GDB syscall packet using snprintf and direct writes into buf; fprintf reports a bad format. Demo writes a PPM header to an opened image file. Shared format_string evidence does not establish comparable buffer roles or bounds guards.

cases.query_anchor: EHCI doesn't handle 16-bit writes to MMIO
cases.demo_anchor: EHCI doesn't handle byte writes to MMIO
cases.note: Both functions reject unsupported EHCI MMIO write widths by logging and exit(1). This is a useful counterexample to automatically discarding every format-only match. No independent relevance score is assigned.
Query creates/registers an opcode table, with error/debug output; demo traverses and prints existing instruction tables. Shared printf is weak evidence for operation and guard comparability.

Query establishes an outgoing connection with EINTR/nonblocking handling; demo binds a multicast socket and joins a group. Both are socket code but shared fprintf does not validate equivalent resource lifecycle or guards.
Query dispatches creation of media streams; demo initializes a QEMU monitor/chardev. Error reporting through fprintf is the only shared active family, so relevance requires closer review.
Although fprintf is the only identical recognized API, pointer_free is also shared through different APIs. Both functions reorder alarm_timers. Do not misclassify this pair as format-family-only.

Unknown sites are assertions; the body also updates indexed entry fields. Assertions must not be promoted to memory sinks simply to increase call-based coverage. Effective guard semantics are not established.
The function asserts a property type and returns a bit mask. Its sole Unknown assert does not imply an unregistered alloc/copy/free helper. This may be outside the current call-sink coverage scope.

The decoder reads and writes through pointers and casted output pointers. It also uses AV_RL16/AV_RL32 and logging. Resolving wrapper names alone cannot cover its direct memory operations; no guard-effectiveness or vulnerability judgment is made.
RENAME appears in the function declaration; the body updates b1[i] using b0[i] and b2[i]. RENAME must not become a global sink API.
The scanner reports uint8_t(...) from an array-pointer parameter declaration. This is not a runtime function call. The body has indexed reads and writes to *current.

The 22 COPY sites expand to field assignments, including pointer-valued fields. This does not establish a bulk buffer copy or deep copy. A global COPY -> buffer_write rule would conflate unrelated macros.

The inventory contains av_log, but this indexed function-pointer invocation is not represented. The name-before-parenthesis scanner cannot resolve this indirect operation. Its actual callee and contract remain unknown.
RENAME chooses function symbols for pointer assignments, under unresolved build conditions. Its presence does not mean any corresponding pixel conversion is executed here.

The code has inline assembly in one build branch and direct dst/src indexing in the fallback. RENAME, MANGLE and ASMALIGN are not substitutes for modeling those operations or resolving build configuration.
Pixel-writing assembly macros appear inside inline asm. Their definitions and register/operand roles are not present in this function. An exact-name memory rule requires additional contract evidence.
Unknown LOG_INT is diagnostic logging; direct array-based dirty-page bookkeeping occurs separately. Treating the logging macro as a sink would not model that operation.

Inline assembly declares an output memory operand and input pixel operands. MOVQ_ZERO/JUMPALIGN do not describe the memory contract by themselves; current callsite evidence does not represent asm memory effects.
